name: Urine output
seoDesc: Urine output: work out urine volume from the time and the fluid intake. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the Urine output calculator the time, the fluid intake, the urine output rate and the five percent body weight and it returns urine volume. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Urine output calculator work?
sections.html:
The Urine output calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports urine volume in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (your patient's age); then you type in the time, the fluid intake, the urine output rate and the five percent body weight.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as ≥18 years and < 18 years. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in hours. The unit chip switches it to any of the 27 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in milliliters. The unit chip switches it to any of the 40 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilograms. The unit chip switches it to any of the 29 supported units.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

One field on this form is a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the Urine output calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Urine volume=time × urine output rate × weight
Urine volume=-fluid balance + fluid intake
Weight=-1 ÷ 50 × five percent body weight

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:

  • Shown in milliliters, and convertible to any of the 40 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Time, opening in hours
  • Volume, opening in milliliters
  • Volume, opening in milliliters
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Volume, opening in milliliters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Urine output calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the time, the fluid intake and the urine output rate — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Urine output calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns urine volume, derived from the time, the fluid intake and the urine output rate. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Urine output calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the time, the fluid intake, the urine output rate and the five percent body weight, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Urine output calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
